Internal helper: the example a recode-family stop gives when no variable is named

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_no_var_example.Rd

One example per function, given by two stops (Session 370, Fix Slate 18): the function's own stop for a data frame named with no variable (.jst_no_var_stop()), and ruling R22's single stop for a call naming neither (.jst_no_frame_stop()), so the two agree. Each is a line on community that runs as printed in every convention state (voice Rule AC; Jeff, S369: a remedy must not lead to another stop). The functions that return a variable are assigned to a column of community, as jsum()'s and javg()'s examples are; jdeclare_missing() names its convention, since a declaration on a plain variable needs one and community's are SPSS-style. community's one text variable is its ID, so jencode()'s example encodes RespondentID.

Usage

.jst_no_var_example(fn)

Arguments

fn

Character. The function's name.

Value

NULL for a function with no entry, else a list: call (the call, quoted), lhs (the column it is assigned to, or NULL), n ("one" or "one or more"), noun (for R22's line, when not "variables"), provide (the no-variable stop's second line, before ", for example:"), named (the arguments that name variables) and keep (the arguments R22's stop keeps from the call).
